ordered_diagnoses: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder

facts.raw_span: 15-year history of Parkinson disease
Hoehn and Yahr score, 3
20-year history of sleep disturbance
worsening dream enactment behavior
daytime motor symptoms improved following deep brain stimulation
episodes of dream enactment became progressively more violent
yelling occurred multiple times per night
violent behaviors were reported every other night
Initial polysomnography demonstrated obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), with an Apnea Hypopnea Index score of 8.5
Emergency department neuroimaging was unremarkable
Repeat polysomnography demonstrated an Apnea Hypopnea Index score of 12.8
one severe episode resulted in a head laceration after striking the wall

concepts.preferred_label: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder
concepts.why: The patient's worsening dream enactment behavior and violent behaviors during sleep episodes are characteristic of REM Sleep Behavior Disorder, which is often associated with Parkinson disease.
The patient's initial and repeat polysomnography results demonstrate obstructive sleep apnea, with Apnea Hypopnea Index scores of 8.5 and 12.8, respectively.
The patient's 15-year history of Parkinson disease, Hoehn and Yahr score of 3, and improvement in daytime motor symptoms following deep brain stimulation are consistent with Parkinson disease.
The patient's 20-year history of sleep disturbance, yelling, and violent behaviors during sleep episodes suggest a sleep disturbance.
The patient's combination of sleep disturbance, dream enactment behavior, and obstructive sleep apnea suggests a complex sleep disorder.
The patient's yelling, violent behaviors, and self-injurious behaviors during sleep episodes are characteristic of a nocturnal behavioral disorder.
The patient's head laceration resulting from a severe episode of dream enactment behavior is an example of a sleep-related injury.
The patient's Parkinson disease and sleep disturbance are related, as sleep disturbances are a common non-motor symptom of Parkinson disease.
It explains the head laceration after striking the wall during a sleep episode.

rationales.F01: The patient's 15-year history of Parkinson disease supports the diagnosis of Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder and Parkinson Disease with Sleep Disturbance.
rationales.F04: Worsening dream enactment behavior is a key feature of Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.
rationales.F06: The progression of dream enactment to violent behaviors is consistent with Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.
rationales.F09: The presence of obstructive sleep apnea is a separate diagnosis from Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder.
rationales.F10: The absence of traumatic brain injury is important to rule out as a cause of sleep disturbance.
rationales.F11: The increase in Apnea Hypopnea Index score supports the diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea.
rationales.F12: The occurrence of self-injurious behaviors during sleep episodes is consistent with Sleep-Related Injury.
